Common Cold.description: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat, usually resolving on its own within 7-10 days.
home_remedies: Sip warm honey and lemon tea to soothe the throat
Inhale steam from a bowl of hot water
Gargle with warm salt water
Rest and drink plenty of warm fluids

Influenza.description: A contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses, more severe than the common cold.
precautions: See a doctor if symptoms worsen
home_remedies: Drink warm fluids like ginger or herbal tea
Take honey to ease cough and sore throat
Use a warm compress for body aches
Rest fully and keep hydrated

COVID-19.description: An infectious disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, affecting the respiratory system with a wide range of severity.
precautions: Seek emergency care for breathing difficulty
home_remedies: Stay well hydrated with warm fluids
Use steam inhalation to ease congestion
Gargle warm salt water for a sore throat
Rest and monitor your symptoms closely

Migraine.description: A neurological condition causing intense, throbbing headaches often with nausea and light sensitivity.
precautions: Rest in a dark, quiet room
home_remedies: Rest in a dark, quiet room
Apply a cold compress to the forehead
Sip water to stay hydrated
Gently massage the temples and neck

Tension Headache.description: The most common type of headache, causing mild to moderate dull, aching pain.
precautions: Apply a warm or cold compress
home_remedies: Apply a warm compress to the neck and shoulders
Practice deep breathing or meditation
Stay hydrated
Take short breaks away from screens

Gastroenteritis.description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, typically due to viral or bacterial infection.
precautions: Stay hydrated with oral rehydration solutions
home_remedies: Sip oral rehydration solution or coconut water
Eat bland foods like bananas, rice, and toast
Drink ginger tea to calm nausea
Rest and avoid dairy

Food Poisoning.description: Illness caused by consuming contaminated food, leading to gastrointestinal distress.
precautions: Rest the stomach with bland foods
Avoid solid food until vomiting stops
Seek care if symptoms are severe
home_remedies: Sip small amounts of water or ORS frequently
Try ginger or peppermint tea for nausea
Eat plain foods once vomiting stops
Rest and avoid solid food early on

Acid Reflux (GERD).description: A digestive disorder where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus.
home_remedies: Sip cold milk or chamomile tea
Chew a small piece of fresh ginger
Avoid lying down for 2-3 hours after meals
Eat smaller, slower meals

Peptic Ulcer.description: Open sores that develop on the inner lining of the stomach or upper small intestine.
home_remedies: Drink cabbage juice or coconut water
Take a little honey on an empty stomach
Avoid spicy and acidic foods
Include probiotic foods like yogurt

Irritable Bowel Syndrome.description: A common disorder affecting the large intestine, causing cramping and altered bowel habits.
home_remedies: Sip peppermint tea to ease cramps
Apply a warm compress to the abdomen
Add fiber-rich foods gradually
Practice stress-reducing relaxation

Urinary Tract Infection.description: An infection in any part of the urinary system, most commonly the bladder and urethra.
precautions: Urinate frequently, don't hold it in
home_remedies: Drink plenty of water to flush the system
Try unsweetened cranberry juice
Apply a warm heating pad to the lower abdomen
Urinate frequently and don't hold it in

Kidney Stones.description: Hard deposits of minerals and salts that form inside the kidneys, causing significant pain when passing.
precautions: Seek medical care for severe pain
home_remedies: Drink lots of water throughout the day
Try lemon water to help break down stones
Apply a warm compress for pain relief
Reduce salt in your diet

Bronchitis.description: Inflammation of the lining of the bronchial tubes, which carry air to and from the lungs.
precautions: See a doctor if cough persists over 3 weeks
home_remedies: Inhale steam to loosen mucus
Drink warm honey and lemon
Use a humidifier at night
Stay hydrated and rest your voice

Pneumonia.description: An infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid.
home_remedies: Rest completely and drink warm fluids
Use steam inhalation to ease breathing
Take warm honey for cough comfort
Seek medical care — home care is only supportive

Asthma.description: A chronic condition in which airways narrow, swell, and produce extra mucus, making breathing difficult.
precautions: Seek emergency care for severe attacks
home_remedies: Sit upright and practice slow breathing
Sip warm water or ginger tea
Avoid triggers like dust and smoke
Keep your rescue inhaler nearby — seek care for severe attacks

Allergic Rhinitis.description: An allergic response causing cold-like symptoms, such as sneezing and a runny nose.
precautions: Keep windows closed during high pollen
home_remedies: Rinse nasal passages with saline
Inhale steam to clear congestion
Try a spoon of local honey
Keep windows closed during high pollen

Sinusitis.description: Inflammation or swelling of the tissue lining the sinuses.
precautions: Apply warm compresses to the face
See a doctor if symptoms persist beyond 10 days
home_remedies: Use steam inhalation with a few drops of eucalyptus
Rinse sinuses with a saline solution
Apply a warm compress to the face
Stay well hydrated

Conjunctivitis.description: Inflammation of the membrane covering the eye, commonly known as pink eye.
precautions: See a doctor if vision is affected
home_remedies: Apply a clean warm or cold compress to the eyes
Rinse eyes gently with cooled boiled water
Avoid rubbing the eyes
Use separate clean towels

Dengue Fever.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing severe flu-like illness.
precautions: Seek immediate care for bleeding or severe pain
home_remedies: Drink plenty of fluids and ORS
Try papaya leaf juice to support recovery
Rest completely
Use acetaminophen for fever, not aspirin — seek care for warning signs

Malaria.description: A mosquito-borne disease caused by a parasite, producing recurring fever and chills.
precautions: Seek medical care immediately for antimalarial treatment
Use mosquito protection to prevent spread
home_remedies: Stay hydrated with fluids and ORS
Rest fully
Use a cool compress for fever
Seek medical care immediately — remedies are only supportive

Typhoid Fever.description: A bacterial infection spread through contaminated food and water, causing prolonged fever.
home_remedies: Drink ORS and plenty of fluids
Eat soft, easily digestible foods
Sip ginger or tulsi (basil) tea
Rest — antibiotics from a doctor are essential

Chickenpox.description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy, blister-like rash.
precautions: Trim nails to reduce skin damage
home_remedies: Take a cool oatmeal or baking soda bath
Apply calamine lotion to reduce itching
Keep nails trimmed to avoid scratching
Wear loose, soft cotton clothing

Measles.description: A highly contagious viral infection of the respiratory system, causing a distinctive rash.
home_remedies: Rest in a comfortable, dimly lit room
Stay hydrated with fluids
Use a cool compress for fever
Eat vitamin A-rich foods — seek medical guidance

Hypertension.description: Persistently elevated blood pressure in the arteries, a major cardiovascular risk factor.
precautions: Monitor blood pressure and take medication as prescribed
home_remedies: Reduce salt and eat potassium-rich foods
Practice deep breathing or meditation
Take regular brisk walks
Limit caffeine and alcohol

Type 2 Diabetes.description: A chronic condition affecting how the body processes blood sugar (glucose).
home_remedies: Include fiber-rich, whole foods
Take a short walk after meals
Stay hydrated with water
Add cinnamon or fenugreek to meals (with your doctor's okay)

Hypothyroidism.description: A condition where the thyroid gland doesn't produce enough thyroid hormone.
precautions: Report new symptoms to your doctor
home_remedies: Eat iodine-rich foods like fish and dairy
Include selenium sources such as nuts
Exercise regularly to boost energy
Take medication consistently as prescribed

Hyperthyroidism.description: A condition where the thyroid gland produces too much thyroid hormone.
home_remedies: Eat calming, balanced meals
Limit caffeine and stimulants
Practice relaxation to manage stress
Ensure you get adequate rest

Anemia.description: A condition marked by a deficiency of red blood cells or hemoglobin, reducing oxygen delivery.
home_remedies: Eat iron-rich foods like spinach and lentils
Pair iron foods with vitamin C for absorption
Include beetroot and dates
Avoid tea or coffee with meals

Anxiety Disorder.description: A mental health condition characterized by persistent, excessive worry.
precautions: Consider speaking with a mental health professional
home_remedies: Practice slow, deep breathing exercises
Try chamomile or green tea
Exercise or take regular walks
Limit caffeine and keep a steady sleep routine

Depression.description: A mood disorder causing persistent feelings of sadness and loss of interest.
precautions: Reach out to a mental health professional
home_remedies: Get regular sunlight and fresh air
Stay physically active
Maintain social connection
Keep a consistent daily routine — seek professional support

Insomnia.description: A sleep disorder characterized by difficulty falling or staying asleep.
precautions: Avoid caffeine late in the day
home_remedies: Drink warm milk or chamomile tea before bed
Keep a consistent sleep schedule
Avoid screens an hour before bed
Try relaxation or light stretching

Eczema.description: A condition that makes skin red, inflamed, and itchy.
home_remedies: Moisturize with a fragrance-free cream
Apply a cool compress to itchy areas
Take lukewarm oatmeal baths
Avoid harsh soaps and known irritants

Psoriasis.description: A skin disease causing red, itchy scaly patches, most commonly on the knees, elbows, and scalp.
precautions: Avoid triggers like stress and injury
home_remedies: Moisturize skin generously
Take lukewarm baths with oatmeal or Epsom salt
Get brief, moderate sunlight
Apply aloe vera to affected areas

Acne.description: A skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells.
precautions: See a dermatologist for persistent acne
home_remedies: Wash the face gently twice daily
Apply aloe vera or a little honey to spots
Avoid touching or picking at the skin
Use a warm compress for painful pimples

Fungal Skin Infection.description: A skin infection caused by fungi, thriving in warm, moist areas of the body.
home_remedies: Keep the affected area clean and dry
Apply plain yogurt or diluted tea tree oil
Wear loose, breathable cotton clothing
Avoid sharing towels and personal items

Rheumatoid Arthritis.description: An autoimmune disorder causing joint inflammation, pain, and swelling.
home_remedies: Apply warm or cold packs to sore joints
Do gentle stretching and low-impact exercise
Add anti-inflammatory foods like turmeric and ginger
Get adequate rest

Osteoarthritis.description: A degenerative joint disease caused by the breakdown of joint cartilage.
precautions: Use joint support aids if needed
home_remedies: Apply heat or cold to painful joints
Do gentle low-impact exercises
Maintain a healthy weight
Try adding turmeric to your diet

Gout.description: A form of inflammatory arthritis caused by excess uric acid, causing sudden, severe joint pain.
home_remedies: Drink plenty of water to flush uric acid
Apply a cold compress to the joint
Eat cherries or drink cherry juice
Avoid alcohol and purine-rich foods

Chronic Fatigue Syndrome.description: A complex disorder characterized by extreme fatigue not explained by an underlying condition.
precautions: Work with a doctor on a management plan
home_remedies: Pace activities and rest between tasks
Keep a consistent sleep routine
Stay hydrated and eat balanced meals
Try light stretching or gentle yoga

Appendicitis.description: Inflammation of the appendix, a medical emergency usually requiring surgery.
precautions: Avoid eating or drinking until evaluated
Do not take laxatives or pain medication that could mask symptoms
home_remedies: Do not eat, drink, or take laxatives
Avoid placing heating pads on the abdomen
Rest and stay still
This is an emergency — go to a hospital immediately
